questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: It is a really fun experience if you manage to get a nice friendgroup. But you have to be welcome to maybe sharing a room and not living in the best of best conditions.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *

questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level is generally a little bit lower, thus for me it was a perfect level of difficulity having to take master classes as a bachelor student.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I prefer the one at UCPH as it is more dynamic. Teaching in Milano is mostly lectures and i thus miss having student exercises along the course.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Molecular Bioinformatics, Communicable and Non-communicale diseases, Additional Skills: Italian, Cell Therapy and Gene-silencing, Molecular pharmacology and immunology.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Cell Therapy and gene silencing, Molecular pharmacology and immunology.

questions.answer: ESN is great in Italy.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I was present at many ESN events, such as bar-evenings, padel tournaments and more.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Join ESN events in the begininning to meet people from other countries.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go on hike in the Como-Lake area! it is really beautiful.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Quite difficult as the italian culture is very different from the danish. The professors and students were always late to lectures - something that is not occuring in Denmark.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The chaotic nature of italians. Everything is very loose which can be an advantage but certainly also a disadvantage. The professors often turn up late as well as the students - even at exames. So make sure that you are open-minded and dont take everything so serious.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer:
The food, trips and scenery is amazing. Also a lot of cool events have occured in or near Milan. I experienced fashion week, ATP finals in Torino, The Olympics, AC vs Inter Milan and many more cool events! 
The weather was also really nice, even in january and february!

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Relax! everything will turn out fine. Make sure to enjoy the time there and dont cheap out on food and experiences! So yes to as much as you can but also remember that it is okay to say no and stay home and relax. 
Try to learn a little bit of italian and speak with the locals, they will love you.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I would definetly recommend trying to meet people from other countries and not only talk with people from Denmark. I did both and got the best of both worlds!

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting people from other countries and the expeirence of living in another country.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The not knowing and feeling like you don't have control of everything going on. Also the FOMO (fear of missing out) is alot and can be challenging while also trying to focus on studies.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
